lines.trans: Every good neighbourhood café needs one hot lunch bowl and one signature cake.
Did we just get promoted to official taste testers, Rami?
Best job in the building! Which bowl do we try first, Salma?
Left spoon: roasted tomato soup with fresh courtyard herbs.
Rich, warm, and great with crusty bread on a rainy afternoon!
Right spoon: golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil—even better!
Now try the two lemon tart slices: thin pastry on the left, almond crust on the right.
Oh—the almond crust with Saturday market lemon is unbeatable!
Save one slice for Tariq, Salma, or he will lock us out of the kitchen!
So Wednesday's menu is set: golden lentil soup, warm bread, almond lemon tart, and tea!
Simple, honest, and easy to serve quickly from noon to evening.
Now let us hope for sunny skies tomorrow so our shutter paint dries!

meanings.note: Praises honest natural materials, authentic recipes, or trustworthy character.

examples.text: الخشب الأصيل بيعيش سنين طويلة لو اعتنينا فيه.
examples.trans: Honest solid wood lasts for decades when cared for.

examples.text: قائمة سلمى بسيطة وأصيلة من خيرات البلد.
examples.trans: Salma's menu is simple and authentic, made with local produce.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Used as a question word or indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.text: كل سبت الصبح بنمشي عسوق الحارة.
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning we walk to the neighbourhood market.

examples.text: الخبز الطازة بيجهز يوم السبت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Fresh bread is ready on Saturday at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بنايات.

examples.trans: The stone building is eighty years old.
The building owner sent a letter.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine collective word for tomatoes (from Italian pomodoro).

examples.trans: The roasted tomato soup smells mouthwatering.

examples.text: اشترينا كيلو بندورة حمرا من سوق السبت.
examples.trans: We bought a kilo of ripe red tomatoes at the Saturday market.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Form V verb meaning 'be promoted to a higher post or role'.

examples.text: نور ترقت وصارت موظفة استقبال رسمية.
examples.trans: Nour got promoted to permanent receptionist.
We got promoted today to café taste testers!

meanings.note: Form V verb; passive/reflexive of قدّم ('serve food/drink').

examples.text: الشوربة السخنة بتتقدم مع خبز محمص.
examples.trans: The hot soup is served with toasted bread.

examples.text: قهوة الصبح بتتقدم بالساحة الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Morning coffee is served in the courtyard at eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتمنى, بيتمنى).

examples.trans: We hope every guest feels comfortable with us.
We wished them a happy trip.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبي, بيخبي).

examples.trans: Why did you save it away for me all these years?
She tucked the recipe away in the kitchen notebook.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.note: Someone with a discerning palate who tests food or tea (plural ذواقة zawwaaqa).

examples.text: رامي وزياد صاروا ذواقة الشوربة والتارت بالكافيه.
examples.trans: Rami and Ziad became the soup and tart tasters for the café.

examples.text: أبوي ذواق قهوة وبيعرف البن الطازة فورا.
examples.trans: My dad is a coffee connoisseur and spots fresh beans right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رسمية, plural: رسميين).

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for the guests only!
An official letter arrived in the noon post.

meanings.note: Describes thin flaky pastry, fine paper, or gentle manners.

examples.text: العجينة الرقيقة طلعت مقرمشة وخفيفة بالفرن.
examples.trans: The thin pastry came out crisp and light in the oven.

examples.text: كتب الملاحظة على ورق رقيق بقلم رصاص.
examples.trans: He wrote the note in pencil on thin paper.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian, رهيب / رهيبة enthusiastically praises food or ideas ('amazing, terrific!').

examples.text: الزبدة المالحة رهيبة مع البيض المقلي!
examples.trans: Salted butter is terrific with fried eggs!
Salma's morning coffee is amazing.

meanings.note: Usually implies olive oil in Jordan unless specified otherwise, but used for all oils.

examples.text: حطينا نقطتين زيت على كل مفصلة حديد.
examples.trans: We put two drops of oil on every iron hinge.

examples.text: شوربة العدس بتطلع أطيب مع رشة زيت زيتون.
examples.trans: Lentil soup tastes even better with a drizzle of olive oil.

meanings.note: Collective noun for olives, iconic to Jordanian tables and courtyards.

examples.text: فطور الصبح ما بيكمل بدون زيت وزيتون أخضر.
examples.trans: Morning breakfast isn't complete without olive oil and green olives.

examples.text: شجرة الزيتون بآخر الحارة عمرها مية سنة.
examples.trans: The olive tree at the end of the lane is a hundred years old.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماوات.

examples.trans: The evening sky is clear and calm.
The lanterns are glowing beneath the sky.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'easy to do'.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة سهلة وبتجهز بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: This recipe is easy and comes together in half an hour.

examples.text: سهل نرتب الكراسي بعد ما يخلص الدهان.
examples.trans: It will be easy to arrange the chairs once the painting is done.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسواق.

examples.text: سوق وسط البلد مليان حركة الصبح.
examples.trans: The downtown market is bustling in the morning.
We bought fresh herbs from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Versatile spoken Levantine noun meaning 'task / job / matter'.

examples.text: ضل علينا تلات شغلات بسيطة قبل يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: We only have three simple tasks left before Wednesday.

examples.text: تذوق الكيك هو أحلى شغلة بالكافيه كله!
examples.trans: Tasting cake is the best job in the entire café!

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شوربات.

examples.trans: Here is a cup of hot vegetable soup.
Hot soup is wonderful on a rainy day.

meanings.note: Levantine word for slatted window shutters, used as a collective: الشيش مسكر 'the shutters are closed'.

examples.trans: Close the shutters, the sun is strong.
Green shutters suit the house.

meanings.note: Everyday word for both a dinner plate and a teacup saucer (صحن الفنجان).

examples.text: رتبت سلمى اتنعش صحن أبيض جنب الفناجين.
examples.trans: Salma arranged twelve white saucers next to the cups.

examples.text: حطي الكيك السخن بصحن كبير عالطاولة.
examples.trans: Put the warm cake on a big plate on the table.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: Used for fresh food, produce, or bread.

examples.text: خبز سلمى طازة وسخن كل صبح.
examples.trans: Salma's bread is fresh and hot every morning.

examples.text: اشترينا ليمون طازة ونعنع أخضر من السوق.
examples.trans: We bought fresh lemons and green mint from the market.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: Used for baking dough.

examples.trans: The bread dough is ready in the oven.
She left the dough to rest half an hour.

meanings.note: Collective noun; شوربة عدس ('golden lentil soup' with lemon and olive oil) is a beloved Jordanian staple.

examples.text: شوربة العدس مع عصرة ليمون أطيب غدا بالشتا.
examples.trans: Lentil soup with a squeeze of lemon is the best lunch on a rainy day.

examples.text: سلمى غسلت العدس الأصفر وحطته عالنار.
examples.trans: Salma rinsed the yellow lentils and set them on the stove.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أعشاب.

examples.trans: We sprinkled green herbs on top of the eggs.
Tariq grows fresh herbs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Cozy Levantine word for the pleasant late-afternoon tea/coffee hours.

examples.text: قعدة العصرية بالساحة مع الشاي ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard in the late afternoon with tea is unbeatable.

examples.text: خبز محمص وشوربة دافية بعصرية ماطرة إشي رائع.
examples.trans: Crusty bread and warm soup on a rainy afternoon are wonderful.

meanings.note: The main meal of the day in Jordan, usually eaten in the early afternoon.

examples.trans: What's for lunch today?
We have lunch together after work.

meanings.note: Describes a wealthy person as well as rich flavours, colours, or musical tones (طعم غني 'rich taste').

examples.text: عسل الجبل طعمه غني ودافي مع الشاي.
examples.trans: Mountain honey has a rich, warm taste with tea.

examples.text: خشب الجوز بيعطي البيانو صوت غني.
examples.trans: Walnut wood gives the piano a rich sound.

meanings.note: A written list or a restaurant menu; with -i it is قائمتي, 'my list'.

examples.trans: I wrote the shopping list before the market.
May I have the menu?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Singulative of collective قشر ('peel, bark, shell'); قشرة الليمونة means 'the skin/zest of the lemon'.

examples.text: قشرة الليمون الأصفر ريحتها قوية وحلوة.
examples.trans: Yellow lemon peel has a strong, sweet scent.

examples.text: بتحط سلمى برش قشرة ليمون بعجينة الكيك.
examples.trans: Salma puts grated lemon peel into the cake batter.

meanings.note: Used to count items, or mean a portion, slice, or spare part.

examples.trans: Please have a piece of warm bread.

examples.text: خبزت كيكة مع قطع زوايا زيادة.
examples.trans: She baked a cake with extra corner pieces.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقفل, بيقفل).

examples.trans: We locked your suitcase safe in the storage closet.
I lock the iron gate at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كافيهات.

examples.trans: We opened a small café in the house courtyard.
The morning café serves all the neighbours.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Chiefly used in ما إله / ما إلها مثيل ('unmatched / unbeatable').

examples.text: خبز سلمى السخن الصبح ما إله مثيل بالحارة.
examples.trans: Salma's warm bread in the morning has no equal in the neighbourhood.

examples.text: ليمون سوق السبت ريحته وطعمته ما إلهم مثيل.
examples.trans: The scent and flavour of Saturday market lemons are unbeatable.

meanings.note: Used to describe a neat person, a well-organized room, or generally something of high quality (e.g. 'a nice car').

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting right away.
Neat pencil sketches.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Describes weather or a place receiving plenty of sunlight.

examples.trans: Please sit beside the sunny window.
The sunny attic room overlooks the courtyard.

meanings.note: Passive participle of شوى ('roast/grill').

examples.text: البندورة المشوية بالفرن بتعطي الشوربة طعمة غنية.
examples.trans: Oven-roasted tomatoes give the soup a rich flavour.

examples.text: ريحته زاكية مع خضار مشوية وزيت زيتون.
examples.trans: It smells delicious with roasted vegetables and olive oil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Favorite Levantine food word for crusty fresh bread or crisp pastry.

examples.text: الخبز طلع من الفرن سخن ومقرمش.
examples.trans: The bread came out of the oven hot and crusty.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز المقرمشة أطيب إشي بالتارت.
examples.trans: The crisp almond crust is the best part of the tart.

meanings.note: In spoken Jordanian, standard ملعقة shifts consonants to معلقة (ma'laqa), plural معالق (ma'aaliq).

examples.text: حطي معلقة صغيرة جنب كل فنجان.
examples.trans: Put a small spoon beside every cup.
The silver spoons are in the top drawer.

meanings.note: Describes a rainy day, season or night (يوم ممطر 'a rainy day').

examples.trans: It was a cold, rainy day.
Winter this year is very rainy.

meanings.note: Describes a café's signature dish (كيكة مميزة) or a special occasion.

examples.text: كل كافيه ناجح عنده كيكة مميزة بيعرفوها الناس.
examples.trans: Every great café has one signature cake people know it for.

examples.text: يوم الافتتاح رح يكون يوم مميز للكل.
examples.trans: Opening day is going to be a special day for everyone.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb (nishif / byinshaf) meaning 'dry out'.

examples.text: لما تطلع الشمس، الحجار بتنشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: When the sun comes out, the stones dry quickly.

examples.text: استنينا ساعتين لحد ما ينشف الدهان.
examples.trans: We waited two hours until the paint dried.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Introduces a playful warning or consequence ('or else…').

examples.trans: Drink your coffee now or else it'll go cold!

examples.text: خبي قطعة تارت لطارق وإلا بيزعل منا!
examples.trans: Save a slice of tart for Tariq or else he'll be cross with us!

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; وجه لوجه means 'face to face'. Plural: وجوه.

examples.trans: They stood face to face under the tree.
The top of the cake turned golden in the oven.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.
